Debug and release focused runs twice; strict all-target Clippy; isolated compiled mutation; source syntax twice.
cost: Validation O(V+E), then at most V rounds each cloning V entries and inspecting V+E data: O(V(V+E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space. Costs include an empty-edge graph. No timing claim.
forward: Reject an invalid source first, then the first invalid endpoint in row/edge order. On valid graphs return None exactly at unreachable vertices and Some of the minimum walk weight elsewhere, unless a source-reachable negative cycle exists, which returns ReachableNegativeCycle. All signed i64 edge weights, duplicates, loops and disconnected components are supported. i128 checked addition returns DistanceOverflow if representation fails; on current <=64-bit usize targets at most V edges per synchronous round fit i128.
2026-10-30 deep graph epoch: see specialized relations in adjacent model.md and six deterministic source tests.
inverse: Let X be allocated finite adjacency vectors with i64 weights and usize sources, and Y the typed Result<Vec<Option<i128>>,BellmanFordError> observation space, excluding allocation failure and nontermination. Let R subset X times Y be the graph of the Forward relation including source-before-edge validation and first checked-overflow precedence. Define U=X times Y and behavior_complement=U minus R. Thus every input has its unique permitted observation in R; all other typed observations are in the complement. The shortest-walk characterization assumes representable synchronous sums (guaranteed on current <=64-bit usize targets). Finite negative fixtures check selected memberships, not this whole universe.

Given successful vector d, compatible antecedents are all validated graphs and valid sources whose reachable minimum walk weights equal d and have no reachable negative cycle. Many graphs fit the same d: unused edges may change while preserving minima. InvalidSource recovers source>=V; InvalidEdge recovers a valid source and first offending edge; ReachableNegativeCycle recovers existence and source reachability, not its unique vertices. DistanceOverflow describes first failed checked sum.
limitations: Partial syntax has no macro expansion or type resolution. Bounded evidence is not proof. Allocation failures are outside the Result contract. No approximate executable profiles.
